title: The Sacrifice of the Son
subtitle: Genesis 22 · Jubilees 17–18 · Qur'an 37:99–113
summary: A source-anchored comparison across biblical, Second Temple Jewish, and Quranic accounts of Abraham's ultimate trial, mapping narrative slots, textual differences, pairwise relations, and distinct reception histories.

slots.label: The Trial Initiated
slots.description: How the command to offer the son originates and is delivered to Abraham.

genesis-22.summary: God directly tests Abraham, commanding him to offer Isaac in the land of Moriah as a burnt offering.
genesis-22.verbatimExcerpt: After these things, God tested Abraham, and said to him, "Abraham!" He said, "Here I am." He said, "Now take your son, your only son, whom you love, Isaac, and go into the land of Moriah. Offer him there for a burnt offering on one of the mountains which I will tell you of."
genesis-22.limits: No heavenly antagonist is mentioned; the initiative is stated solely as God testing Abraham.

jubilees-17-18.summary: Prince Mastema challenges God in heaven regarding Abraham's devotion; God then commands Abraham to offer Isaac on the mountain.
jubilees-17-18.verbatimExcerpt: And the prince Mastêmâ came and said before God, 'Behold, Abraham loves Isaac his son, and he delights in him above all things else; bid him offer him as a burnt-offering on the altar, and Thou wilt see if he will do this command, and Thou wilt know if he is faithful in everything wherein Thou dost try him. And God said to him, 'Abraham, Abraham'; and he said, Behold, (here) am I.' And he said, Take thy beloved son whom thou lovest, (even) Isaac, and go unto the high country, and offer him on one of the mountains which I will point out unto thee.'
jubilees-17-18.limits: Distinguishes Mastema's instigation from God's command; God already knew Abraham's faithfulness across prior trials.

quran-37.summary: Abraham tells his son he has seen in a dream that he must sacrifice him, and asks for the son's counsel.
quran-37.verbatimExcerpt: And when he was old enough to work with him, he said: O my dear son, I have seen in a dream that I must sacrifice thee. So look, what thinkest thou? He said: O my father! Do that which thou art commanded. Thou wilt find me, if Allah will, of the steadfast.
quran-37.limits: The trial is presented through a vision/dream (al-manām); the son is not explicitly named in the verse.

slots.label: The Ascent & The Son's Role
slots.description: The journey to the place of sacrifice and the exchange between father and son.

genesis-22.summary: Isaac carries the wood and asks where the lamb is; Abraham answers that God will provide the lamb.
genesis-22.verbatimExcerpt: Abraham took the wood of the burnt offering and laid it on Isaac his son. He took in his hand the fire and the knife. They both went together. Isaac spoke to Abraham his father, and said, "My father?" He said, "Here I am, my son." He said, "Here is the fire and the wood, but where is the lamb for a burnt offering?" Abraham said, "God will provide himself the lamb for a burnt offering, my son." So they both went together.
genesis-22.limits: The text does not state Isaac's age or explicit verbal consent/passivity; they walk 'together'.

jubilees-17-18.summary: Abraham lays the wood on Isaac; Isaac asks where the sheep for the offering is, and Abraham answers that God will provide.
jubilees-17-18.verbatimExcerpt: And he took the wood of the burnt-offering and laid it on Isaac his son, and he took in his hand the fire and the knife, and they went both of them together to that place. And Isaac said to his father, 'Father;' and he said, 'Here am I, my son.' And he said unto him, 'Behold the fire, and the knife, and the wood; but where is the sheep for the burnt-offering, father?' And he said, 'God will provide for himself a sheep for a burnt-offering, my son.' And he drew near to the place of the mount of God.
jubilees-17-18.limits: Follows Genesis narrative closely; emphasizes drawing near to 'the place of the mount of God'.

quran-37.summary: The son explicitly consents: 'O my father! Do that which thou art commanded. Thou wilt find me, if Allah will, of the steadfast.' Both submit.
quran-37.verbatimExcerpt: And when he was old enough to work with him, he said: O my dear son, I have seen in a dream that I must sacrifice thee. So look, what thinkest thou? He said: O my father! Do that which thou art commanded. Thou wilt find me, if Allah will, of the steadfast. Then, when they had both surrendered (to Allah), and he had flung him down upon his face,
quran-37.limits: Focuses on mutual submission (aslamā); does not narrate the 3-day travel itinerary or servants.

slots.label: The Binding & Intervention
slots.description: The moment of sacrifice and the divine voice halting the act.

genesis-22.summary: Abraham builds the altar, binds Isaac, and takes the knife; Yahweh's angel calls from heaven to stop him.
genesis-22.verbatimExcerpt: They came to the place which God had told him of. Abraham built the altar there, and laid the wood in order, bound Isaac his son, and laid him on the altar, on the wood. Abraham stretched out his hand, and took the knife to kill his son. Yahweh's angel called to him out of the sky, and said, "Abraham, Abraham!" He said, "Here I am." He said, "Don't lay your hand on the boy or do anything to him. For now I know that you fear God, since you have not withheld your son, your only son, from me."
genesis-22.limits: The angel speaks from heaven declaring that Abraham's fear of God is now known.

jubilees-17-18.summary: Abraham binds Isaac and takes the knife; the angel of the presence stands before Mastema and calls from heaven to stop; Mastema is shamed.
jubilees-17-18.verbatimExcerpt: And he built an altar, and he placed the wood on the altar, and bound Isaac his son, and placed him on the wood which was upon the altar, and stretched forth his hand to take the knife to slay Isaac his son. And I stood before him, and before the prince Mastêmâ, and the Lord said, 'Bid him not to lay his hand on the lad, nor to do anything to him, for I have shown that he fears the Lord.' And I called to him from heaven, and said unto him: 'Abraham, Abraham;' and he was terrified and said: 'Behold, (here) am I.' And I said unto him: 'Lay not thy hand upon the lad, neither do thou anything to him; for now I have shown that thou fearest the Lord, and hast not withheld thy son, thy first-born son, from me.' And the prince Mastêmâ was put to shame; and Abraham lifted up his eyes and looked, and, behold a ram caught . . . by his horns, and Abraham went and took the ram and offered it for a burnt-offering in the stead of his son.
jubilees-17-18.limits: Frames the intervention as a cosmic vindication over Mastema in the presence of the angels.

quran-37.summary: Abraham lays his son face down; God calls out that the vision has been fulfilled, declaring it a clear trial.
quran-37.verbatimExcerpt: Then, when they had both surrendered (to Allah), and he had flung him down upon his face, We called unto him: O Abraham! Thou hast already fulfilled the vision. Lo! thus do We reward the good. Lo! that verily was a clear test.
quran-37.limits: No knife or physical binding described; the test is fulfilled at the point of complete surrender.

slots.label: The Ransom / Substitute
slots.description: What replaces the son as the sacrifice.

genesis-22.summary: A ram caught in a thicket by its horns is offered as a burnt offering in place of Isaac.
genesis-22.verbatimExcerpt: Abraham lifted up his eyes, and looked, and saw that behind him was a ram caught in the thicket by his horns. Abraham went and took the ram, and offered him up for a burnt offering instead of his son. Abraham called the name of that place "Yahweh Will Provide". As it is said to this day, "On Yahweh's mountain, it will be provided."
genesis-22.limits: Identifies the animal specifically as an ayil (ram).

jubilees-17-18.summary: A ram is offered in Isaac's stead; the place is identified explicitly with Mount Sion.
jubilees-17-18.verbatimExcerpt: And the prince Mastêmâ was put to shame; and Abraham lifted up his eyes and looked, and, behold a ram caught . . . by his horns, and Abraham went and took the ram and offered it for a burnt-offering in the stead of his son. And Abraham called that place 'The Lord hath seen', so that it is said in the mount the Lord hath seen: that is Mount Sion.
jubilees-17-18.limits: Explicitly equates the mountain of the test with Mount Zion (Jerusalem temple mount).

quran-37.summary: The son is ransomed with a 'tremendous victim' (dhibḥ ʿaẓīm).
quran-37.verbatimExcerpt: Then We ransomed him with a tremendous victim.
quran-37.limits: The text does not specify the animal species (e.g. ram); later tradition supplies this detail.

slots.label: Covenant Promise & Subsequent Birth
slots.description: The divine response following the trial and the covenant blessings.

genesis-22.summary: God swears by Himself to multiply Abraham's seed as the stars and sand; all nations on earth will be blessed.
genesis-22.verbatimExcerpt: and said, "'I have sworn by myself,' says Yahweh, 'because you have done this thing, and have not withheld your son, your only son, that I will bless you greatly, and I will multiply your offspring greatly like the stars of the heavens, and like the sand which is on the seashore. Your offspring will possess the gate of his enemies. In your offspring will all the nations of the earth be blessed, because you have obeyed my voice.'"
genesis-22.limits: The blessing is confirmed to Isaac as Abraham's 'only son' present at the scene.

jubilees-17-18.summary: God reiterates the multiplication blessing; institutes a seven-day annual festival of the Lord written on heavenly tablets.
jubilees-17-18.verbatimExcerpt: And he said: 'By Myself have I sworn, saith the Lord, Because thou hast done this thing, And hast not withheld thy son, thy beloved son, from Me, That in blessing I will bless thee, And in multiplying I will multiply thy seed As the stars of heaven, And as the sand which is on the seashore. And thy seed shall inherit the cities of its enemies, And in thy seed shall all nations of the earth be blessed; Because thou hast obeyed My voice, And I have shown to all that thou art faithful unto Me in all that I have said unto thee: Go in peace.' And he celebrated this festival every year, seven days with joy, and he called it the festival of the Lord according to the seven days during which he went and returned in peace. And accordingly has it been ordained and written on the heavenly tablets regarding Israel and its seed that they should observe this festival seven days with the joy of festival.
jubilees-17-18.limits: Provides liturgical etiology for the Passover/Feast of Unleavened Bread timing.

quran-37.summary: Peace is bestowed upon Abraham; afterward, good tidings of the birth of Isaac as a righteous prophet are announced.
quran-37.verbatimExcerpt: And We left for him among the later folk (the salutation): Peace be unto Abraham! Thus do We reward the good. Lo! he is one of Our believing slaves. And We gave him tidings of the birth of Isaac, a prophet of the righteous. And We blessed him and Isaac. And of their seed are some who do good, and some who plainly wrong themselves.
quran-37.limits: The tidings of Isaac's birth following the sacrifice narrative led classical Islamic scholars to debate whether the sacrificed son was Ishmael or Isaac.

edges.basisNote: Jubilees directly reworks the Genesis 22 narrative (Rewritten Bible genre), framing the trial within a heavenly prologue involving Prince Mastema (analogous to Satan in Job 1-2) and establishing a calendar festival.
citations: James L. Kugel, *The Bible As It Was* (Harvard University Press, 1997), 160-176.
Michael Segal, *The Book of Jubilees: Rewritten Bible, Redaction, Ideology and Theology* (Brill, 2007).

edges.basisNote: Qur'an 37 shares the core Semitic narrative of Abraham's willingness to sacrifice his son and the divine substitution, but recasts the episode around active filial consent and visionary dream revelation, with Isaac's announcement following in verse 112.
citations: Reuven Firestone, *Journeys in Holy Lands: The Evolution of the Abraham-Ishmael Legends in Islamic Exegesis* (SUNY Press, 1990).
Angelika Neuwirth, *The Qur'an and Late Antiquity: A Shared Heritage* (Oxford University Press, 2019).

edges.basisNote: Both texts reflect Late Antique/Second Temple developments emphasizing the willing participation and virtue of the righteous son and the test as a vindication of steadfast faith, though with independent literary histories.
citations: Sidney H. Griffith, *The Bible in Arabic: The Scriptures of the 'People of the Book' in the Language of Islam* (Princeton University Press, 2013).

receptionClaims.subject: Isaac as Type of Christ
receptionClaims.text: Early Christian patristic and liturgical commentary read Isaac carrying the wood to Moriah as a prefiguration of Christ carrying the cross to Golgotha, and the substitute ram as a figure of the sacrificial Lamb of God.
receptionClaims.limit: Typological hermeneutic developed in the New Testament and patristic period; not a literal claim of the Genesis text itself.

receptionClaims.subject: The Merit of the Aqedah (Binding)
receptionClaims.text: Rabbinic traditions developed the doctrine of Zekhut Avot (Merit of the Fathers) through the Aqedah, depicting Isaac not as a child but as a willing adult (age 37 in Midrashic chronology) who actively offered his neck to be bound.
receptionClaims.limit: Extends beyond the silence of the Genesis text regarding Isaac's age and internal thoughts.

receptionClaims.subject: The Sacrificed Son (Dhabih) & Eid al-Adha
receptionClaims.text: Islamic tradition commemorates Abraham's trial during the annual Hajj pilgrimage and Eid al-Adha. Classical exegetes (Tabari, Ibn Kathir) recorded dual early traditions regarding whether the sacrificed son was Ishmael (the consensus view) or Isaac.
receptionClaims.limit: Qur'an 37 does not explicitly name the youth in verses 102-107, leading to early interpretive differences before Ishmael became the normative consensus.

provenance.reviewScope: Jubilees quotations and the ram-offering summary corrected against the 1913 printed text; existing narrative alignment, rights, and reception separation retained. See docs/jubilees-source-review.md.
